title: UnDercontrol Dataflow
description: A dataflow diagram, via 'ud apply -f'. Uses the YAML envelope format (apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec). A diagram is a record, not a file: the graph JSON lives in the diagram itself and the name carries no '.dataflow.json' suffix. Identity is (owner, path, name), enforced as unique by the server, so a document with no 'metadata.id' still updates the diagram it names rather than creating a second one — the same file can be edited and re-applied indefinitely. Applying unchanged content writes nothing at all: the server compares a hash of the graph and treats a match as a no-op, so no version is recorded and the update timestamp does not move.

metadata.description: 'metadata.id' names an existing diagram directly and takes precedence over the (path, name) key; omit it and the key decides. 'metadata.tags' sets the diagram's tags.

name.description: The diagram's name, without a file extension — a suffix is an artefact of being a file, and this is not one. Together with 'path' it forms the identity a re-apply resolves against, so changing it creates a new diagram rather than renaming this one unless 'metadata.id' is also given.

path.description: Virtual folder the diagram appears under in the explorer tree. Part of the identity key: the same name under two paths is two diagrams. Defaults to the root.

data.description: The graph as JSON text, stored byte for byte. The graph JSON must be the full graph format — nodes carry 'type' + 'data' (+ optional 'id', 'position', 'style'), and pipes/edges reference node ids — and this is the ONLY format of 'data'. The retired simplified ({name, fields} nodes) and architecture (top-level 'groups' key) dialects are rejected by the editor's import. 'position' is optional, all-or-nothing: omit it on every node and the editor computes the layout, then a saved diagram materializes the result as plain coordinates; a partially positioned graph is not solved (unpositioned nodes land at the origin). MUST be written as a YAML block scalar ('data: |'), never spread into a YAML mapping: YAML decoding rewrites values on the way through — a leading zero is read as octal (0755 becomes 493), a trailing zero is dropped (1.10 becomes 1.1), and a bare run of digits stops being a string. The last one is the dangerous case, because the JSON text is identical either way and only the type changed. The graph is always inline here: a manifest describes the state a diagram should be in, and a path that only resolves on one machine is not part of that state. (An earlier 'dataFile' field held such a path; a document still carrying it is refused with the substitution to use, rather than ignored.) Images must be referenced as resources ('resourceId' or 'resource://<uuid>'); a graph containing an inline 'data:' URI is rejected regardless of its size, and one version of a graph may not exceed 1 MiB.

entity_type.description: Attach the new diagram to something as it is created — 'todolist' for a task. Only read on create; use the attachment endpoints to change it afterwards.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity named by 'entity_type'. Quote it: an all-digit short id is a YAML integer when bare.

metadata.description: Extensible key-value store carried with the diagram.

identity_and_idempotency.description: (owner, path, name) is unique in the database, not merely by convention in the CLI. A create that would collide with an existing diagram is refused rather than silently updating it; 'ud apply' resolves the key first and issues an update when it hits, which is what makes re-applying an edited document update one diagram instead of growing a second.

versions.description: Every write that actually changes the graph snapshots the previous content as a version, and versions are kept indefinitely. Changing only the name, path, tags or metadata does not record one — versions track the picture, not its labels. Restoring a version writes it back as a new revision rather than erasing what came after it, so the state you rolled away from remains in the history.

images.description: A picture inside a diagram is a resource referenced by id, never bytes embedded in the graph. It therefore has its own owner, its own sharing state and its own lifecycle: deleting the diagram does not delete it, and it can be removed independently, at which point the node renders as unavailable.

storage_accounting.description: A diagram's bytes live in the record, not in object storage, and do not count against the storage quota — the quota is object storage's ledger. This holds for the versions too.
